title: Newton's second law of motion
body:
Newton's second law states that the net force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration: F = m * a. Force is measured in newtons, where one newton accelerates a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s².

A 70 kg sprinter accelerating at 3 m/s² needs a net force of 210 N. The law explains why heavier objects need more force to reach the same acceleration.

title: Kinetic energy
body:
Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its motion. It is given by E = 0.5 * m * v^2, where m is the mass and v is the velocity. Doubling the speed quadruples the kinetic energy.

A 1000 kg car moving at 20 m/s carries 200000 J of kinetic energy, which the brakes must turn into heat to stop it.

title: Ohm's law
body:
Ohm's law relates voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit: V = I * R. Voltage is measured in volts, current in amperes, and resistance in ohms.

A 9 V battery driving current through a 450 Ω resistor produces a current of 0.02 A. Engineers use the law to size resistors so that components receive a safe current.

title: The Pythagorean theorem
body:
In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: c = sqrt(a^2 + b^2). The theorem is one of the oldest results in mathematics, known to Babylonian scribes long before Pythagoras.

A triangle with sides of 3 and 4 units has a hypotenuse of 5 units. The theorem underlies distance calculations in geometry, navigation, and computer graphics.

title: Photosynthesis
body:
Photosynthesis is the chemical reaction plants use to turn light energy into chemical energy. Inside the chloroplasts of each cell, carbon dioxide and water combine to form glucose and oxygen. The overall reaction uses six molecules of carbon dioxide and six of water for every molecule of glucose.

Photosynthesis supplies almost all of the oxygen in the atmosphere and the energy at the base of most food chains.

title: Wave speed
body:
The speed of a wave equals its frequency times its wavelength: v = f * lambda. Sound in air at room temperature travels at about 343 m/s, so a 343 Hz tone has a wavelength of 1 m.

Light follows the same relationship, with the speed of light c = 299792458 m/s in a vacuum.
